title: outage-scenario-sweep-and-atomic-restore-audit
creator: Samantha Li
description:
Goal: Produce a reproducible outage-scenario sweep and an atomic-restore audit that proves Redwood can meet target RTO/RPO for active-passive deployments. Scope includes: SLO alignment for cross-region failover, circuit-breaker behavior under progressive load-shedding, backup snapshot integrity checks, and an automated verification harness to run scheduled failovers without manual orchestration.

Objectives:
- Define target SLOs for public endpoints and internal RPCs during and after failover (primary targets: 99.9% availability for control-plane routes, P95 latency degradation <2x for metadata operations).
- Create a matrix of outage scenarios (network partition, primary region full-gone, degraded KV store, partial quorum loss) and expected system behaviors and rollback gates.
- Implement an atomic-restore audit that validates snapshot integrity, KV reconciliation, and ordered replay of critical streams (token-store, routing table, rollout state).
- Harden circuit-breaker thresholds and staged load-shedding policies so passive region promotion does not cascade into overload.
- Deliver an executable schedule for weekly automated sweeps and quarterly high-fidelity manual exercises with clear preflight checks and postmortem anchors.

Acceptance criteria:
- A runnable test harness (k8s job + playbook) that executes 6 canonical scenarios and reports pass/fail on KV consistency, request routing, and service health.
- A documented checklist with preflight probes, blast-radius controls, and rollback commands in the Console.
- SLO post-exercise report published to the reliability dashboard with token-level cost and latency impact.
- PRs merged for monitoring queries and automated runbook steps.

Non-goals: full rewrite of autoscaler logic; modelling every third-party failure modality (we'll simulate third-party latency via fault injection).

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Passive region can become overloaded during promotion. Mitigation: implement staged LB weight ramp with per-route circuit breakers and backpressure tokens.

Risk: Snapshot drift between primary and passive for KV leads to inconsistency. Mitigation: include snapshot checksum verification and a deterministic replay layer; fail the drill if divergence > 500ms of writes to critical namespaces.
Risk: Client-side retries amplify traffic during failover. Mitigation: recommend client SDK backoff policy and server-side short-lived 429s with Retry-After headers to coordinate ramp.
Risk: Blindly failing over during partial network partitions causing split-brain. Mitigation: quorum checks + enforced lease semantics in control plane before promotion.
metrics_and_slo_mapping: Control-plane health: route-registration success rate -> target 99.9% during sweep
Token-store RTO: restore to read-write -> target <= 3m for warm-standby, <= 15m for cold restore
KV-consistency: tail divergence window -> target <= 1s for critical namespaces
P95 request latency for admin RPCs -> allowed degradation <2x during failover
Error budget consumption reported per-exercise in the reliability dashboard
